description:
About the job

The Buyer is the strategic sourcing engine of the brand, reporting directly to the Head of Supply Chain. From day one, this role is responsible for optimizing the current product catalog, reducing costs without compromising the sensory identity of the product, and sustaining inventory availability in a fast-paced growth environment. The Buyer owns the end-to-end purchasing relationship with suppliers, the logistics of getting production out the door (case pack definition, forwarder quoting, and pick-up coordination), and the sourcing of new suppliers whenever current partners fall short of the brand's quality, cost, or service expectations. The Buyer will work in close collaboration with S&OP and Demand Planning, and will serve as the technical-commercial link between suppliers and business objectives. This is not an administrative role: it is a role with direct impact on margin, collection launches, and brand positioning.




Key Responsibilities:




Supplier Management:




Manage a portfolio of domestic and international suppliers (contract manufacturing, raw materials, and packaging).
Maintain up-to-date supplier scorecards tracking reliability, quality, lead time, and pricing.
Identify and onboard new suppliers aligned with brand standards, including cruelty-free and sustainability criteria.
Proactively source and vet alternative suppliers whenever a current supplier fails to meet the brand's expectations on quality, cost, lead time, or reliability, and lead the transition to the replacement.
Build and manage long-term supplier relationships without compromising negotiating power.




Purchasing & Outbound Logistics Coordination:




Place and follow up on purchase orders with suppliers, confirming pricing, quantities, specifications, and delivery dates.
Define case pack configurations with suppliers (units per case, carton dimensions and weight, palletization) to optimize shipping efficiency and warehouse handling.
Request and compare quotes from freight forwarders (ocean, air, and ground) to select the most cost-effective and reliable routing for each production run.
Coordinate and schedule pick-ups with forwarders directly from supplier facilities, ensuring all export documentation is complete and on time.
Track shipments from origin to destination, flagging delays and coordinating with the Logistics team on customs clearance and receiving.
Maintain a rolling log of freight costs and forwarder performance to inform future routing and negotiation decisions.




Negotiation & COGS Reduction:




Negotiate payment terms, volumes, and pricing under a win-win approach.
Identify cost-saving opportunities through order consolidation or material substitution.
Develop Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analyses by SKU and product line.
Report monthly procurement KPIs including savings vs. budget variance.




S&OP Collaboration:




Actively participate in the monthly S&OP cycle, providing visibility into lead times and supply risks.
Coordinate purchase orders aligned with demand plans and seasonal collection calendars.
Anticipate stock-out risks on critical SKUs and activate contingency plans proactively.
Manage the campaign and collection buying calendar to ensure on-time sourcing.
Support the new product launch pipeline with timely and strategic sourcing.




Technical Profile — Hard Skills




· Procurement experience: 3–5 years (cosmetics, pharmaceutical, or retail industry preferred)

· Advanced Excel (pivot tables, logical formulas, cost modeling)

· ERP / procurement systems (SAP, Odoo, Oracle or equivalent)

· Procurement KPI analysis and reporting

· Fill rate, lead time tracking, and savings measurement

· Working knowledge of Incoterms, export documentation, case pack/carton optimization, and freight forwarder quoting and coordination (ocean, air, and ground)

· Sensitivity: Pantone references, paper weights, finishes, and packaging standards

· English Level: Professional proficiency in reading, writing, and verbal communication for business and procurement contexts.




Soft Skills




· Persuasive negotiation: Ability to close win-win agreements under time and cost pressure without damaging commercial relationships.

· Sharp attention to detail: Ability to detect potential deviations in quality, packaging, or procurement processes before they impact the brand.

· Agility & adaptability: Ability to respond swiftly to trend shifts or supply chain disruptions without losing operational momentum.

· Assertive communication: Direct interaction with founders, senior leadership, and suppliers; ability to build compelling arguments and deliver difficult messages clearly.

· Ethics & sound judgment: Make sourcing decisions that reflect the brand’s commitment to sustainability, cruelty-free standards, and ethical supply chain practices.

· Sense of urgency: Startup mindset — builds processes while executing them, without being paralyzed by ambiguity or incomplete information.
